scene: A phone vlog in the car park of a big stadium on a bright autumn morning, hours before an American football game: the tailgate party. Pick-up trucks, grills smoking, people chatting and laughing some way off. Luna holds the phone at arm's length and talks to it while she holds up the one flat sandwich they brought; Timo stands upright just behind her.
context: A twenty-second comedy sketch played by two close friends who bicker. It must sound like two real people talking, quick and natural, never like an advert or a narrator. LUNA, about 25, is cheerful and quick; she is proud of the one sandwich they brought and gossips happily to the camera about Timo, who she thinks is sulking somewhere; by the end she is small and hopeful. TIMO, about 30, is slow, dry and proud; he never raises his voice; today he is calm and quietly pleased with himself, because a stranger with a grill has made friends with him, and he states each thing as a plain fact. They answer each other fast, with no gaps between the lines.
lines: [bright, to the camera, proud of the sandwich] American football! The tailgate! We brought a sandwich.
[lower, confiding to the camera, amused] Timo hates it. He says it's just a car park—
[cutting in, calm and level, right behind her] Gary says hello.
[flat, as if that explains everything] Gary has a grill.
[accusing but fond] You don't like people.
[a plain fact, quietly proud] He's invited me for Thanksgiving.
[after a beat, small and hopeful, not looking up] Can I come?
[flat and final, to the camera] It's a family thing.

L.audio_profile: A cheerful woman of 25 with a bright, warm, quick voice; standing in a busy open car park on a crisp morning, speaking up a little over the chatter, pleased with herself; natural and unpolished, like a friend filming a vlog.

T.audio_profile: A tall, calm man of 30 with a low, dry, casual voice; slow, proud, deadpan and quietly content; he never raises his voice.
